title: Green Snap Beans, Canned, Regular Pack, Drained Solids

content.title: About
content.content: Green snap beans in a can are a preserved vegetable made from fresh beans that have been blanched and then drained. The product is ready to eat, offering a tender‑crisp texture and a mild sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Snap beans belong to the legume family and are a good source of plant protein.
Canning locks in nutrients for up to 2‑3 years of shelf life.
In the United States, canned green beans are a common ingredient in hot‑dogs and salads.
The beans are typically heat‑treated at 115 °C for 30‑45 minutes during processing.
Draining the liquid after opening reduces the sodium content.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned green beans provides about 8 g of protein, useful for vegetarians.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The beans contain folate, thiamine, and vitamin B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They provide iron, magnesium, and potassium, contributing to overall health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned snap beans contain virtually no saturated fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned versions often contain added salt; draining the liquid can lower sodium intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination after opening
items.content: Once opened, store the beans in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑4 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned green beans can be eaten straight from the can, tossed into salads, soups, pasta dishes, or used in a warm side dish. Usually the brine is drained and the beans are rinsed with cold water before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer the beans to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
